High-stakes continental football took center stage as Platense hosted Independiente Santa Fe in a clash that promised tactical intrigue and physical intensity. Both sides entered the fray knowing that every moment would be crucial in their pursuit of CONMEBOL Libertadores glory. A Cagey Opening Exchange The encounter on April 29, 2026 , began with both teams displaying a cautious approach, prioritizing defensive solidity over expansive attacking play. The atmosphere was thick with tension, which translated into a series of physical challenges early in the first half . Victor Leandro Cuesta was the first to see yellow in the 13th minute as Santa Fe struggled to contain the home side's transitions. Platense soon followed suit with Ivan Gomez receiving a booking, and the half continued to be defined by its stop-start nature. Luis Palacios also found his way into the referee's book before the break, as neither side managed to carve out a definitive opening, leaving the game scoreless at the interval. Mainero Sparks the Second Half Explosion The complexion of the match shifted dramatically following a double substitution at the start of the second half . While the first period was characterized by attrition, the second became a showcase for the vision of Guido Mainero . In the 57th minute, Mainero delivered a pinpoint ball to find Tomas Nasif , who made no mistake in slotting home the opening goal . The breakthrough energized the home crowd and rattled the visitors, who picked up another booking through Kilian Toscano just moments later as they attempted to regain their footing. Platense refused to let their momentum slip, and it was Mainero once again who proved to be the architect of Santa Fe's undoing. Only six minutes after the opener, he provided his second assist of the evening, this time setting up Mateo Mendia . Mendia’s clinical finish in the 63rd minute doubled the lead and seemingly put the result beyond doubt. The double-salvo forced the visitors into a flurry of substitutions, bringing on the likes of Jhojan Torres and Nahuel Lautaro Bustos in a desperate attempt to salvage a result. Late Drama and the Final Whistle As the clock wound down, the intensity rose once more. Santa Fe pushed forward with increased urgency, leading to a late yellow card for Daniel Torres and a frantic series of tactical changes from both dugouts. Just as the fourth official signaled for stoppage time, the visitors finally found a breakthrough. In the 94th minute, Emanuel Olivera turned provider for Franco Fagundez , who found the net to set up a nervous final few minutes for the home side. Despite the late pressure and the narrow margin, Platense held firm through seven minutes of added time. The referee’s final whistle confirmed a hard-fought victory for the hosts, rewarding their clinical edge in the second half and leaving Santa Fe to rue a period of defensive lapses that cost them dearly on the night.
